Metformin XR — Bioequivalence Safe Space & VBE Error Rate (PBPK)

Reference formulation: T50 = 3.0 h

Author

Nikita

Published

June 9, 2026

Background

This report defines the bioequivalence (BE) safe space of metformin extended-release (XR) formulations from a validated PK-Sim PBPK model (Open Systems Pharmacology metformin model). Formulation behaviour is varied through the in-vivo dissolution half-time T50: small T50 releases fast (higher, earlier Cmax); large T50 releases slowly.

The reference formulation is T50 = 3.0 h; every other formulation (T50 = 1, 2, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7 h) is a test product assessed against it.

Two analyses are reported:

  1. Point average BE — the regulatory CI-based decision: BE if the 90% CI of the GMR for both Cmax and AUC lies within 80–125%.
  2. Virtual BE (VBE) — resampled n-subject crossover trials give the probability a real study concludes BE. This curve is the safe space; in truly non-equivalent regions its value is the Type I error (consumer risk).

Design and settings

  • Paired crossover. PK-Sim simulates the same virtual individuals (IDs 0–23) under every formulation → a fully paired 2×2 crossover (no period/sequence effect); we analyse within-subject log-differences (TOST).
  • VBE: 500 replicate trials; study sizes n = 48 and 86 subjects. Limitation: the PBPK population has 24 unique virtual subjects, so n>24 trials bootstrap with replacement from those 24 physiologies (between-subject diversity is capped at 24).
  • Metric note. For XR products with heavy AUC extrapolation we lead with AUC0-t. AUC∞ is reported but unreliable for slow-release arms (long terminal t½ → large, uncertain extrapolation → wide CIs).
  • Tooling. Julia + open Pumas-ecosystem packages (DataFrames, CSV, CairoMakie). Licensed Pumas Bioequivalence/NCA can be swapped in once the env is instantiated with a JuliaHub token; base-R scripts under programs/R are an independent cross-check (agree to all digits).

PK metrics by formulation

Inference. Cmax falls monotonically as release slows (29.8 → 13.6 µmol/L), so it is the BE-determining endpoint. AUC0-t falls gently; AUC∞ is flat then inflates for the slow arms (flip-flop kinetics) — a numerical artefact of extrapolation, not extra exposure.

1. Point average BE (90% CI decision)

Inference. The decision is CI-based, not point-GMR-based. Cmax drives both edges: fast release (1.0 h) breaches the upper limit (GMR 1.36, CI 131.9–139.9%); slow release (≥5.0 h) breaches the lower limit. AUC0-t fails only at the slow extreme; AUC∞ shows spuriously wide CIs at 6–7 h from extrapolation. Formulations passing both Cmax and AUC0-t: T50 = 2.0, 3.0 (ref), 3.5, 4.0 h.

2. Within-subject variability (sourced)

Metformin is a low-variability drug. Intra-subject CVs adopted for the VBE simulation (extended-release):

Inference. Because intra-subject CV is low (~11–12%), a modest study (n = 24–48) already has high power to detect equivalence near the reference — the safe-space edges are therefore set by the true formulation difference (Cmax vs T50), not by trial noise.

3. VBE safe space by endpoint (500 trials; n = 48 and 86)

The safe space is the T50 band where a trial reliably (power ≥ 80%) concludes BE. Green = safe, red = fail; open circles are the 8 simulated formulations; the curve interpolates each subject’s response between them.

Cmax (BE-determining endpoint)

Inference. Cmax gives the narrowest safe space (n=48: 2.00–4.15 h; n=86: 1.80–4.25 h), so it governs the overall decision. Increasing n from 48→86 widens the band only slightly (≈0.3 h) — consistent with low intra-subject CV: power near the edges is already high, and the edges are driven by the true GMR crossing 80/125%, which more subjects cannot move.

AUC0-t

Inference. AUC0-t is more permissive (≈1.0–4.6/4.7 h): exposure changes less than peak with release rate, so only the slow extreme fails. It never limits the joint decision on the fast side.

AUC∞

Inference. AUC∞ appears widest (≈1.0–5.0 h) but this is not reliable: for slow arms the long terminal t½ forces heavy, uncertain extrapolation (and dropped subjects at 7 h), inflating the GMR and CI. AUC∞ should not drive the XR safe space — use AUC0-t.

Joint decision (Cmax & AUC0-t)

Inference. The regulatory safe space is the joint pass region, which equals the Cmax band (Cmax is limiting): n=48 ≈ 1.95–4.10 h, n=86 ≈ 1.85–4.25 h around the 3.0 h reference.

Safe-space boundaries and VBE pass-rates

Inference. Pass-rates are ~100% inside the safe space and collapse to 0–0.6% at the truly non-equivalent slow arms (6–7 h) — Type I error is well controlled (≤ 5%). The borderline arms (5 h AUC) show the expected power gain with n (e.g. AUC∞ 78.6% → 96.0%).

Conclusions

  • Reference: T50 = 3.0 h.
  • Point-BE safe set (simulated formulations): T50 = 2.0, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0 h (Cmax & AUC₀-t, 90% CI ⊂ 80–125%).
  • Continuous VBE safe space (joint, power ≥ 80%): ≈ 1.9–4.1 h (n = 48), 1.85–4.25 h (n = 86).
  • Cmax is the BE-determining endpoint; AUC0-t and (artefactually) AUC∞ are more permissive.
  • Larger study size (48 → 86) widens the safe space only marginally — a signature of metformin’s low intra-subject variability; the edges are set by the true formulation effect, not trial noise.
  • Type I error is controlled (≤ 5%) at truly non-equivalent formulations.

Next steps (per MAP)

  • Fit the PopPK model to a sparsely-sampled, residual-error version of these PBPK profiles, repeat this VBE workflow, and overlay the PBPK vs PopPK safe-space curves (decision equivalence).
  • Add the IR high-variability (≈23.7%) scenario to bracket the safe space under higher CV.
